correctness.rationale: The loss identity is S'=-kappa*rho_00. If a positive trajectory had a positive limiting trace, a nonzero positive accumulation state would evolve at constant trace. Positivity eliminates its hub row and column, and g!=0 then forces the leaf block to annihilate the all-ones vector. Its leaf Hamiltonian consequently commutes with it, and the leaf off-diagonals decay at rate delta. In the limit the diagonal block still annihilates the all-ones vector, so it is zero, a contradiction to the constant positive trace. Since positive matrices linearly span the full matrix space, finite-dimensional semigroup convergence on positive inputs gives negative spectral abscissa; no dilation is needed. Permutation symmetry allows a uniform mixture for the survival trace of a localized input. In the reduced system q=(kappa+delta)/2 and Delta=epsilon-(n-1)h. The integrated hub population, leaf off-diagonal and imaginary hub–leaf coherence are 1/kappa, -1/(n*delta), -1/(2*g*n), respectively; the real coherence integral is Delta/q times the imaginary one. Substitution into the imaginary-coherence equation yields exactly the stated T. At fixed kappa, T'' in delta is 2(n-1)/delta^3+2 Delta^2/[g^2(kappa+delta)^3]>0 and T diverges at both endpoints. At resonance the rate optimization separates; at zero dephasing the norm squared of the invariant dark projection is 1-1/n, while the bright–hub sector decays because g!=0. Twelve independently assembled full Liouvillian inversions for n=2,3,4,5,7 agreed to maximum absolute error 1.07e-14, and bounded direct minimizations agreed with the resonant rates and a detuned stationarity root. The all-time trajectories and the optimization path at fixed physical controls need not coincide with the uniform-noise model.

evidence: Write q=(kappa+delta)/2 for the audited model and q'=kappa/2+delta for prior uniform dephasing at lambda=delta and prior amplitude-trap rate kappa'=kappa/2. With N=n+1, S=1 and Gamma=0, the inverse rate from prior Eqs. (21)–(23) is N/kappa+(N-2)/delta+q'/(2J^2)+(Delta')^2/(2J^2*q'). The efficiency is one at positive dephasing and no background loss (also follows from the same constant-trace argument as for leaf-only dephasing).

Choose J=|g|*sqrt(q'/q) and prior detuning Delta'=Delta*q'/q by setting its hub energy to (N-2)J+Delta'. The sign of g is immaterial by rephasing the hub. This is an actual integrated-system correspondence: leave the integrated hub population, common leaf population and common leaf–leaf coherence unchanged, and multiply both integrated hub–leaf quadratures by sqrt(q/q'). The population and leaf-coherence equations contain the same product J times the new imaginary quadrature; the last two zero-frequency equations, whose initial-coherence sources vanish, are both multiplied by sqrt(q'/q). Thus the survival integrals agree. The prior formula with this substitution gives exactly the four terms of the Finding for all positive rates, without assuming h=g in the audited dynamics.

Strict convexity, the fixed-sink stationarity equation and the separated resonant minimum are immediate derivatives/minimizations of this implied expression. At delta=0 the dark projection depends only on the uniform hub-coupling direction, as in the earlier complete-network dark-state calculation, not on h.

evidence: With no background decay and unit trapping probability, the conditional first moment of sink flux used by Alterman et al. equals the survival integral in the Finding. Their population loss is 2 times their parameter kappa, and uniform dephasing lambda damps both leaf–leaf and hub–leaf coherences at lambda before adding the trap damping.
The symmetric system depends on h and epsilon only through the bright-state detuning. The detuned complete graph has that same detuning parameter independently tunable by its hub shift.
The 50%-capture observable in the extended-star paper is a median, not an equivalent formulation of a first moment.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Time integration, unit flux, permutation averaging and the factor-of-two loss convention must all be matched before converting the prior transfer rate to mean time. Leaf-selective noise does change trajectories; the exact equivalence is at zero frequency for the localized-start observable.

evidence: No matching numerical catalogue is needed for this continuous-parameter problem; the relevant exact material is formula-level. The October 26 Resultary finding is an exact match at h=epsilon=0 and zero hub dephasing. The October 18 finding has noise at the hub as well and a different linear dephasing coefficient; the same-day result treats coherent weak disorder and gives a different decay law.
The original complete-network formula is an exact formula covering arbitrary detuning after converting the parameters, rather than a finite table at selected rates.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A table of sample trapping times cannot resolve an all-parameter first-moment formula and extrema. The closely indexed analytic cases were compared by observable, dephasing placement and Hamiltonian, not just by date or shared quantum-star terminology.

originality.rationale: The physical dynamics have a different local dephasing convention, but the claimed integrated observable reduces exactly to the previously evaluated uniform fully connected mean-time observable of Alterman, Berman and Strauch. The reduction is a rescaling of the two integrated hub–leaf coherences with the corresponding hopping and detuning substitutions, valid at every declared parameter point. The optimizers in the Finding follow by elementary differentiation of that implied formula. There is no claim of full time-domain equivalence.
residual_risks: Pouthier 2015 was unavailable in full; the exact priority of specialized-star statements is not determined. The arXiv version of Alterman et al. supplies the displayed formulas used in the positive coverage argument regardless of availability of the journal PDF.
